newsitem.title: USA: Radisys CFO says lawsuit has no merit.
newsitem.headline: Radisys CFO says lawsuit has no merit.

text.p: Radisys Corp Chief Finacial Officer Brian Turner said Monday a lawsuit against the company alleging financial misrepresentation has no merit.
Turner also said the maker of computer chips for telecommunication and medical devices has not been contacted by the Securities and Exchange Commission in relation to the lawsuit.
"The company believes the lawsuit has no substance and we will vigorously fight it," Turner said.

In July, Bruce Taylor, former Radisys vice president of operations, filed a suit against Radisys alleging that he told other executives of "significant discrepancy in the financial records" and was fired shortly thereafter.
In a letter to Taylor's attorney obtained by Reuter, the Securities and Exchange Commission also asked Taylor to provide information and voluntary testimony for an "informal inquiry" into Radisys.

Turner said the SEC has not yet contacted Radisys and he knows of no inquiry. An SEC spokesman declined to say whether the company is under an inquiry. Taylor also could not immediately be reached for comment.
Radisys stock plunged 19 percent Monday after an article in today's issue of Barron's highlighted charges in the lawsuit.
Turner said Radisys had disclosed the lawsuit to investors in July. He said he was calling investors to tell them "there is no new news and nothing has changed."
